claims.statement: Across (state, primary, signal), the Blackwell capture ratio correlates more with AUROC than with ECE (Spearman)

claims.verdict_rule: declared pooled diagnostic: task-bootstrap CI of |Spearman(capture_bw, AUROC)| - |Spearman(capture_bw, ECE)| over all (state, primary, signal) rows: PASS if > 0, FAIL if < 0, else INCONCLUSIVE; the within-(state, primary) refinement and the native-usage variant are reported alongside, not used for the verdict

claims.statement: A calibrated but uninformative signal (Z permuted within state) has net VOI ~ -k: its gross VOI is ~0 and never significantly positive
claims.verdict_rule: share of rows whose permuted gross VOI has a 95% CI above 0 must not exceed the nominal one-sided rate 2.5%, median |capture_perm| <= 0.02, mean net/k at k=0.01b within 10% of -1. CAVEAT: the first draft of this script demanded zero such rows; with >3,000 simultaneous intervals that is unattainable by chance and was replaced by the nominal-rate rule before the README was written

claims.statement: cor:info-vs-proposer: at equal cost, buying exact routing information beats upgrading the primary iff b*Delta p < a(1-s); sign agreement on decided (state, primary, upgrade) rows

The negative capture of the five classical routers (X3 Table, pooled, Qwen3-Max, theta=1, Z = chose the primary) is reproduced and explained: P(H=1|Z=0) > a/b, so their native rule sends sufficient tasks to Opus that the uninformed cascade would have attempted; the Blackwell-optimal use of the same Z is never negative
